title: Arthur Ashe Stadium Undergoes Renovations During 2024 US Open
seoTitle: Arthur Ashe Stadium Renovations at 2024 US Open
subtitle: Details on the construction transforming New York's premier tennis stage
excerpt: Arthur Ashe Stadium, the main US Open arena, is undergoing renovations during the tournament, bringing new areas and improvements for players and fans.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The US Open tennis tournament began with matches on Sunday, but spectators noticed changes at the event's most iconic venue. Arthur Ashe Stadium, host of the finals, is undergoing extensive renovations, part of a three-year project that already exceeds the $800 million mark.

Renovations underway at Arthur Ashe Stadium

The works include the addition of seats in the lower bowl of the arena, upgrades to entertainment areas, and the construction of an athlete performance center. A sign at the entrance indicates that the stadium is being "reimagined."

Impact on early matches

Even with the renovations, the tournament proceeded on schedule. The first day of play brought the historic first-round elimination of Novak Djokovic, in a match that lasted over four and a half hours. Play was interrupted when the retractable roof of Arthur Ashe Stadium was closed due to rain.

First winners and interesting facts

Jessica Pegula won the first match in the stadium, while Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk highlighted the advantage of playing on Sunday, gaining more rest time before the second round. Other highlights included victories by Elina Svitolina, Jasmine Paolini, and Leylah Fernandez.

Technical issues and weather

In addition to the rain that forced the roof to close, there was a mechanical failure in a sensor at Louis Armstrong Stadium, requiring the court to be dried before the match between Alexander Bublik and J.J. Wolf. Seven matches were not completed due to the bad weather.

Expectations for the coming days

With the renovations progressing, the US Open continues to attract big names like Aryna Sabalenka, Carlos Alcaraz, and Daniil Medvedev, who has already won his first match in the competition. Players and the public can expect a modernized environment as the tournament advances to the decisive stages.

With information from the Orlando Sentinel.
